title.en: Tetralogy of Fallot: four features one repair

idea.en: Name all four features and show each on the echo.

label.en: Malaligned septal defect with aortic override

note.en: Branch pulmonary arteries for size and confluence

steps.en: What you see: Four features travel together: a malaligned ventricular septal defect with the aorta overriding the septum, right ventricular outflow obstruction with a small pulmonary annulus, right ventricular hypertrophy with a thick wall, and an overriding aorta straddling the septum. The outflow gradient sets the degree of cyanosis. Unrepaired adults show collaterals and a boot shaped cardiac silhouette on the chest radiograph.

Normal values with units: Pulmonary annulus size. Compare with the aortic annulus in the same study. A pulmonary annulus clearly smaller than the aortic annulus with a high outflow gradient marks significant obstruction.. Source: ASE 2019 transthoracic examination guideline, section on parasternal short axis views

Outflow peak gradient. Higher gradients mean less pulmonary flow and deeper cyanosis. Record the peak gradient in mmHg by four times velocity squared with the velocity in m per s.. Source: ASE 2019 transthoracic examination guideline, section on Doppler and haemodynamics

Right ventricular wall thickness. Normal free wall 5 mm or below at end diastole. Above this the ventricle is hypertrophied from pressure load.. Source: ASE 2019 transthoracic examination guideline, section on the right ventricle

ECG and heart sound correlation ecg: Right axis deviation with right ventricular hypertrophy marks pressure load. Right bundle branch block appears after repair. Atrial arrhythmia follows late after repair in adult survivors.

ECG and heart sound correlation sounds: A harsh ejection systolic murmur at the upper left sternal edge marks outflow turbulence. The second sound is single with a loud aortic component. Cyanotic spells in unrepaired severe disease in infancy are a paediatric emergency.

analogy.en: Landmarks: Malaligned septal defect with aortic override

spot.en: Landmarks: Malaligned septal defect with aortic override
Branch pulmonary arteries for size and confluence
What to report: Defect size and position with the degree of aortic override
Outflow anatomy at every level with annulus sizes and peak gradient
Right ventricular thickness and function with branch artery sizes
Coronary pattern, duct status and collaterals for the surgical plan
Red flags needing urgent referral: Cyanotic spell in an infant, needs immediate paediatric cardiology care with knee chest positioning and oxygen
Duct dependent circulation in a neonate, needs urgent prostaglandin and surgical review
Polycythaemia with stroke or brain abscess in an unrepaired patient, needs urgent combined care
Pitfalls: Spells ease with squatting and worsen with crying or dehydration, so record triggers in the history.
Iron deficiency worsens spells, so check haemoglobin in every cyanotic child.
After repair, pulmonary regurgitation with right ventricular dilatation drives late referral, so follow right heart sizes lifelong.
Figure: Parasternal long axis shows the malaligned defect with aortic override above the septum. View tte_plax

todo.en: How to get it on the probe, step by step: Start in the parasternal long axis and find the defect with the aorta overriding the septum.
Measure the override and note which great vessel arises from which ventricle.
Move to the outflow view and measure the pulmonary annulus and main trunk.
Record continuous wave Doppler across the outflow for the peak gradient.
Assess right ventricular wall thickness, branch pulmonary arteries and any duct or collaterals.

Common mistakes and how to correct them: Missing the defect by scanning one plane only. Fix: Sweep from long axis to short axis at the base. Doubly committed defects sit just below the valves and hide in one plane.
Underreading the outflow gradient with an off axis beam. Fix: Measure in systole with the beam parallel to the outflow. Off axis beams underread the gradient.

Ignoring coronary anomalies that cross the surgical field. Fix: Map coronaries before any intervention is planned, since an anomalous left anterior descending artery crosses the outflow in some patients.

remember.en: Recognise spells and duct dependence as emergencies.

q.en: Which combination defines tetralogy of Fallot?

o.en: Isolated septal defect with normal outflow
Malaligned defect with override plus outflow obstruction plus hypertrophy plus overriding aorta
Isolated valve stenosis with a normal septum

why.en: All four features travel together: malaligned defect, outflow obstruction, hypertrophy and an overriding aorta.

q.en: What does a rising outflow gradient do to cyanosis?

why.en: Less blood reaches the lungs as obstruction rises, so right to left shunting and cyanosis deepen.

q.en: An infant has a prolonged cyanotic spell. What next?

why.en: Spells can be fatal and need immediate paediatric cardiology care with oxygen and volume.

q.en: Which comparison best shows the outflow hypoplasia?

o.en: The pulmonary annulus against the aortic annulus

why.en: A pulmonary annulus clearly smaller than the aortic annulus marks the hypoplastic outflow.
